modules.scoreosis.codec:
-- Canonical, exact encoding of plain Lua data, shared by game clients and the
-- Scoreosis verifier. Numbers round-trip bit for bit; table keys are sorted,
-- so equal states always encode to equal strings.
local M = {}

local floor, frexp, ldexp, format = math.floor, math.frexp, math.ldexp, string.format
local concat, sort, byte, sub, find = table.concat, table.sort, string.byte, string.sub, string.find
local TWO53 = 9007199254740992
local NEG_ZERO = -1 / math.huge

local function encode_number(x)
	if x ~= x then return "N" end
	if x == math.huge then return "I" end
	if x == -math.huge then return "J" end
	if x == floor(x) and x > -TWO53 and x < TWO53 then
		if x == 0 and 1 / x < 0 then return "m" end
		return "i" .. format("%.0f", x) .. ";"
	end
	local m, e = frexp(x)
	return "f" .. format("%.0f", m * TWO53) .. "," .. format("%.0f", e - 53) .. ";"
end

local function key_less(a, b)
	local ta, tb = type(a), type(b)
	if ta ~= tb then return ta < tb end
	return a < b
end

local encode_value

local function encode_table(t, out, depth)
	if depth > 64 then error("codec: nesting too deep") end
	local keys = {}
	for k in pairs(t) do
		local kt = type(k)
		if kt ~= "string" and kt ~= "number" then error("codec: unsupported key type " .. kt) end
		keys[#keys + 1] = k
	end
	sort(keys, key_less)
	out[#out + 1] = "{"
	for i = 1, #keys do
		local k = keys[i]
		encode_value(k, out, depth)
		encode_value(t[k], out, depth)
	end
	out[#out + 1] = "}"
end

function encode_value(v, out, depth)
	local tv = type(v)
	if tv == "number" then
		out[#out + 1] = encode_number(v)
	elseif tv == "string" then
		out[#out + 1] = "s" .. #v .. ":" .. v
	elseif tv == "boolean" then
		out[#out + 1] = v and "t" or "b"
	elseif tv == "table" then
		encode_table(v, out, depth + 1)
	else
		error("codec: unsupported value type " .. tv)
	end
end

function M.encode(v)
	local out = {}
	encode_value(v, out, 0)
	return concat(out)
end

local function read_until(s, pos, ch)
	local stop = find(s, ch, pos, true)
	if not stop then error("codec: truncated input") end
	return sub(s, pos, stop - 1), stop + 1
end

local decode_value

function decode_value(s, pos, depth)
	local tag = sub(s, pos, pos)
	pos = pos + 1
	if tag == "i" then
		local digits, nxt = read_until(s, pos, ";")
		return tonumber(digits), nxt
	elseif tag == "f" then
		local body, nxt = read_until(s, pos, ";")
		local comma = find(body, ",", 1, true)
		return ldexp(tonumber(sub(body, 1, comma - 1)), tonumber(sub(body, comma + 1))), nxt
	elseif tag == "m" then
		return NEG_ZERO, pos
	elseif tag == "N" then
		return 0 / 0, pos
	elseif tag == "I" then
		return math.huge, pos
	elseif tag == "J" then
		return -math.huge, pos
	elseif tag == "t" then
		return true, pos
	elseif tag == "b" then
		return false, pos
	elseif tag == "s" then
		local len, start = read_until(s, pos, ":")
		local n = tonumber(len)
		return sub(s, start, start + n - 1), start + n
	elseif tag == "{" then
		if depth > 64 then error("codec: nesting too deep") end
		local t = {}
		while sub(s, pos, pos) ~= "}" do
			if pos > #s then error("codec: truncated input") end
			local k, v
			k, pos = decode_value(s, pos, depth + 1)
			v, pos = decode_value(s, pos, depth + 1)
			t[k] = v
		end
		return t, pos + 1
	end
	error("codec: bad tag at " .. (pos - 1))
end

function M.decode(s)
	local v, pos = decode_value(s, 1, 0)
	if pos ~= #s + 1 then error("codec: trailing data") end
	return v
end

-- Polynomial checksum mod 2^31-1; exact in doubles, needs no bit library.
function M.checksum(s)
	local h = 7
	for i = 1, #s, 64 do
		local chunk = { byte(s, i, i + 63) }
		for j = 1, #chunk do h = (h * 257 + chunk[j]) % 2147483647 end
	end
	return h
end

-- Inputs travel as "count:bits,count:bits" run-length pairs, one bitmask per tick.
function M.encode_inputs(ticks)
	local out, run, last = {}, 0, nil
	for i = 1, #ticks do
		local bits = ticks[i]
		if bits == last then
			run = run + 1
		else
			if last then out[#out + 1] = run .. ":" .. last end
			last, run = bits, 1
		end
	end
	if last then out[#out + 1] = run .. ":" .. last end
	return concat(out, ",")
end

return M
modules.script.ai:
-- Pure snake-AI helpers ported from godot/sneak/scripts/main.gd.
-- valid_fn(x, y) -> bool is supplied by the controller (bounds + self + obstacles).
local M = {}

-- up, down, left, right (matches the Godot iteration order)
local DIRS = { {x=0,y=-1}, {x=0,y=1}, {x=-1,y=0}, {x=1,y=0} }

-- Choose the snake's next step. It still pursues the target (greedy Manhattan), but it
-- now looks ONE step ahead so it doesn't blunder into a dead-end and box itself in.
-- Each valid candidate is scored (LOWER is better):
--   dist * 3      primary pull toward the target (keeps the snake threatening)
--   - exits * 2   prefer destinations with more forward exits (don't trap yourself)
--   - smooth      tiny bonus for continuing straight (fewer needless wrong turns / jitter)
--   + 1000 (trap) a dead-end -- no forward exit -- is near-suicide; only taken if forced
-- Deliberately a 1-step lookahead, not a full flood-fill: cheap, and imperfect on purpose
-- so a player can still corner the snake into a stuck-death. Returns nil only when boxed in.
function M.choose_move(head, target, facing, valid_fn)
  local best, best_score
  for _, mv in ipairs(DIRS) do
    local nx, ny = head.x + mv.x, head.y + mv.y
    if valid_fn(nx, ny) then
      local dist = math.abs(nx - target.x) + math.abs(ny - target.y)
      local exits = 0
      for _, d2 in ipairs(DIRS) do
        local ex, ey = nx + d2.x, ny + d2.y
        if not (ex == head.x and ey == head.y) and valid_fn(ex, ey) then exits = exits + 1 end
      end
      local smooth = (mv.x == facing.x and mv.y == facing.y) and 1 or 0
      local score = dist * 3 - exits * 2 - smooth + ((exits == 0) and 1000 or 0)
      if not best_score or score < best_score then best_score = score; best = mv end
    end
  end
  return best
end

return M
modules.script.difficulty:
-- Difficulty pacing curve.
-- Replaces the Godot original's straight-linear (level-1) ramp with an
-- upward-trending sawtooth: WAVE-1 levels of rising tension, then a "rest beat"
-- where difficulty dips for a breather, with each cycle peaking higher than the
-- last. Keeps players in the flow channel (tension/release) instead of a grind.
local M = {}

M.WAVE = 4      -- levels per tension cycle (3 up + 1 reset)
M.REST = 0.55   -- valley floor climbs by REST*WAVE each cycle

-- Difficulty "units" for a level. Level 1 = 0 (easiest). Drives speed + length.
function M.units(level)
  local L = math.max(0, level - 1)
  local w = math.floor(L / M.WAVE)
  local p = L - w * M.WAVE
  return w * M.WAVE * M.REST + p
end

return M
modules.script.game_config:
-- Pure gameplay constants ported from godot/sneak/scripts/game_config.gd.
-- No engine deps: safe to require from logic modules and headless tests.
local M = {}

M.CELLS_X = 9
M.CELLS_Y = 15
M.CELL_SIZE = 80
M.HUD_HEIGHT = 80

M.BASE_SNAKE_SPEED = 1.0
-- Tuned for human play. The Godot original used INTERVAL 0.15 / INCREMENT 0.2,
-- which makes the snake tick ~7 Hz at level 1 and ~15 Hz late — faster than a
-- human can react. A difficulty sim (tools/sim_difficulty.js) showed those
-- numbers; these give ~4 Hz early rising to a ~5.5 Hz cap. Length/vision/curve
-- are unchanged — only the snake's MOVE cadence is tamed.
M.SNAKE_SPEED_INCREMENT = 0.08
M.SNAKE_LOST_PLAYER_DURATION = 2.0
M.SNAKE_STUCK_THRESHOLD = 5

M.PLAYER_START_X = 4
M.PLAYER_START_Y = 4
M.SNAKE_START_X = 4
M.SNAKE_START_Y = 8

M.BASE_FOOD_DAMAGE_THRESHOLD = 10
M.MAX_SCORES_SAVED = 10
-- Depth-weighted scoring: a chop is worth ATTACK_SCORE_MULTIPLIER * level and
-- clearing a level pays CLEAR_BONUS * level, so GOING DEEP — not grinding an early
-- level — is what tops the leaderboard. BOTH food and chop score are capped per
-- level (FOOD_SCORE_CAP / CHOP_SCORE_CAP): you get paid to cut the snake down once
-- and to clear, not to farm a regrowing snake on a shallow level. Past the cap
-- they still work (pop segments / progress), they just score 0. Capping food alone
-- left a chop-farm twin (sim + adversarial agent verified); capping both closes it:
-- deep play wins p90 ~238 vs a shallow grinder ~94, and parking is hard-bounded.
M.ATTACK_SCORE_MULTIPLIER = 2
M.CLEAR_BONUS = 10
M.FOOD_SCORE_CAP = 6
M.CHOP_SCORE_CAP = 12
-- Post-chop invulnerability cap (seconds). The original used invuln = level,
-- which at level 10 froze the snake-as-target for 10s and made the level
-- mathematically unwinnable (10 segments x 10s > level time). Capping it keeps
-- the anti-tail-spam purpose while letting late levels be cleared. (sim-verified)
M.INVULN_MAX = 2.0

-- Snake move timer base: wait = clamp(MOVE_INTERVAL / snake_speed, MIN, inf).
-- MOVE_INTERVAL_MIN caps the top speed so late levels never become inhuman.
M.MOVE_INTERVAL = 0.28
M.MOVE_INTERVAL_MIN = 0.18

-- Delay after a snake dies before the next level spawns
M.LEVEL_TRANSITION_DELAY = 2.0

M.VISION = { CONE = 1, RECTANGLE = 2, SQUARE = 3, LONG_LINE = 4, CROSS = 5 }

return M

-- Obstacle configuration ported from godot/sneak/scripts/obstacle_config.gd.
-- Pure data + helpers, no engine deps.
local M = {}

-- Per-level obstacle configs (levels 1-13). Level 13 is the endless template.
M.configs = {
  {level = 1,  count = 8,  pattern = "corner_shields", avoid_edges = true},
  {level = 2,  count = 10, pattern = "symmetrical",   axis = "horizontal",       avoid_edges = true},
  {level = 3,  count = 12, pattern = "line_barriers",  orientation = "horizontal", avoid_edges = true},
  {level = 4,  count = 10, pattern = "bunkers",        bunker_type = "L",          avoid_edges = true},

  {level = 5,  count = 8,  pattern = "symmetrical",   axis = "vertical",          avoid_edges = true},
  {level = 6,  count = 7,  pattern = "bunkers",        bunker_type = "T",          avoid_edges = true},
  {level = 7,  count = 6,  pattern = "line_barriers",  orientation = "both",       avoid_edges = false},
  {level = 8,  count = 5,  pattern = "scattered",      cluster_size = 2,           avoid_edges = false},

  {level = 9,  count = 6,  pattern = "corner_shields", avoid_edges = false},
  {level = 10, count = 5,  pattern = "bunkers",        bunker_type = "L",          avoid_edges = false},
  {level = 11, count = 5,  pattern = "symmetrical",   axis = "both",              avoid_edges = false},
  {level = 12, count = 4,  pattern = "random",         avoid_edges = false},

  {level = 13, count = 5,  pattern = "corner_shields", avoid_edges = false,        randomize = true},
}

-- Exact level match, else clone the last config (endless mode) with level overwritten.
function M.get_config_for_level(level)
  for _, config in ipairs(M.configs) do
    if config.level == level then return config end
  end

  if #M.configs > 0 then
    local last = M.configs[#M.configs]
    local clone = {}
    for k, v in pairs(last) do clone[k] = v end
    clone.level = level
    return clone
  end

  return {level = level, count = 4, pattern = "random", avoid_edges = false}
end

-- base + randi() % (variation*2+1) - variation  (variation default 2)
function M.randomize_count(base, variation, rng)
  variation = variation or 2
  return base + rng.random(0, variation * 2) - variation
end

return M
modules.script.obstacles:
-- Obstacle generation ported from godot/sneak/scripts/main.gd (lines 339-815).
-- Pure grid-cell placement; all Godot node creation stripped out.
-- Cells are {x=,y=}; spawn_obstacle_at -> append to result list + mark occupied.
local C = require "script.game_config"
local config = require "script.obstacle_config"

local M = {}

local CELLS_X = C.CELLS_X
-- Set per generate() call from the caller's seeded generator (script/rng.lua).
local random
local CELLS_Y = C.CELLS_Y

-- Euclidean distance, matching Godot Vector2.distance_to.
local function dist(a, b)
  local dx = a.x - b.x
  local dy = a.y - b.y
  return math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
end

-- Inclusive integer range, matching Godot randi_range (returns `a` when a > b).
local function randr(a, b)
  if a > b then return a end
  return random(a, b)
end

-- Placement state for one generate() run.
local function new_state(player_start, snake_start)
  return {
    occupied = {},          -- ["x,y"] = true
    positions = {},         -- result list of {x=,y=}
    player_start = player_start,
    snake_start = snake_start,
  }
end

local function key(pos) return pos.x .. "," .. pos.y end

-- Port of is_position_available (main.gd 402-424).
-- Bounds + not already occupied + Euclidean clearance < 2 from player/snake start.
local function is_position_available(s, pos, reserved)
  if pos.x < 0 or pos.x >= CELLS_X or pos.y < 0 or pos.y >= CELLS_Y then
    return false
  end
  if s.occupied[key(pos)] then
    return false
  end
  if reserved then
    for _, r in ipairs(reserved) do
      if r.x == pos.x and r.y == pos.y then return false end
    end
  end
  if dist(pos, s.player_start) < 2 then return false end
  if dist(pos, s.snake_start) < 2 then return false end
  return true
end

-- Port of spawn_obstacle_at: record the cell and mark it occupied.
local function spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
  s.positions[#s.positions + 1] = {x = pos.x, y = pos.y}
  s.occupied[key(pos)] = true
end

-- ============ PATTERN FUNCTIONS ============

local function spawn_random_obstacles(s, count, avoid_edges)
  local attempts = 0
  local spawned = 0
  local max_attempts = count * 10

  while spawned < count and attempts < max_attempts do
    local min_x = avoid_edges and 1 or 0
    local max_x = avoid_edges and (CELLS_X - 2) or (CELLS_X - 1)
    local min_y = avoid_edges and 1 or 0
    local max_y = avoid_edges and (CELLS_Y - 2) or (CELLS_Y - 1)

    local pos = {x = random(min_x, max_x), y = random(min_y, max_y)}

    if is_position_available(s, pos) then
      spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
      spawned = spawned + 1
    end

    attempts = attempts + 1
  end
end

local function spawn_scattered_obstacles(s, count, avoid_edges, cluster_size)
  local clusters = math.ceil(count / cluster_size)
  local spawned = 0

  for _ = 1, clusters do
    local min_x = avoid_edges and 2 or 1
    local max_x = avoid_edges and (CELLS_X - 3) or (CELLS_X - 2)
    local min_y = avoid_edges and 2 or 1
    local max_y = avoid_edges and (CELLS_Y - 3) or (CELLS_Y - 2)

    local center = {x = random(min_x, max_x), y = random(min_y, max_y)}

    for _ = 1, cluster_size do
      if spawned >= count then break end

      local offsets = {
        {x = 0, y = 0}, {x = 1, y = 0}, {x = -1, y = 0},
        {x = 0, y = 1}, {x = 0, y = -1}, {x = 1, y = 1},
        {x = -1, y = -1}, {x = 1, y = -1}, {x = -1, y = 1},
      }

      for _, offset in ipairs(offsets) do
        local pos = {x = center.x + offset.x, y = center.y + offset.y}
        if is_position_available(s, pos) then
          spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
          spawned = spawned + 1
          break
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

local function spawn_center_obstacles(s, count, _avoid_edges)
  local center_x = math.floor(CELLS_X / 2)
  local center_y = math.floor(CELLS_Y / 2)
  local spawned = 0
  local attempts = 0
  local max_attempts = count * 10

  while spawned < count and attempts < max_attempts do
    local range_x = math.floor(CELLS_X * 0.3)
    local range_y = math.floor(CELLS_Y * 0.3)

    local pos = {
      x = random(center_x - range_x, center_x + range_x),
      y = random(center_y - range_y, center_y + range_y),
    }

    if is_position_available(s, pos) then
      spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
      spawned = spawned + 1
    end

    attempts = attempts + 1
  end
end

local function spawn_perimeter_obstacles(s, count)
  local spawned = 0
  local attempts = 0
  local max_attempts = count * 10

  while spawned < count and attempts < max_attempts do
    local edge = random(0, 3)  -- 0=top, 1=right, 2=bottom, 3=left
    local pos

    if edge == 0 then
      pos = {x = random(1, CELLS_X - 2), y = random(0, 2)}
    elseif edge == 1 then
      pos = {x = random(CELLS_X - 3, CELLS_X - 1), y = random(1, CELLS_Y - 2)}
    elseif edge == 2 then
      pos = {x = random(1, CELLS_X - 2), y = random(CELLS_Y - 3, CELLS_Y - 1)}
    else
      pos = {x = random(0, 2), y = random(1, CELLS_Y - 2)}
    end

    if is_position_available(s, pos) then
      spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
      spawned = spawned + 1
    end

    attempts = attempts + 1
  end
end

local function spawn_maze_obstacles(s, count, avoid_edges)
  local spawned = 0
  local attempts = 0
  local max_attempts = count * 20

  while spawned < count and attempts < max_attempts do
    local is_vertical = random(0, 1) == 0
    local min_x = avoid_edges and 1 or 0
    local max_x = avoid_edges and (CELLS_X - 2) or (CELLS_X - 1)
    local min_y = avoid_edges and 1 or 0
    local max_y = avoid_edges and (CELLS_Y - 2) or (CELLS_Y - 1)

    if is_vertical then
      local x = random(min_x, max_x)
      local start_y = random(min_y, max_y - 2)
      for dy = 0, 2 do
        local pos = {x = x, y = start_y + dy}
        if is_position_available(s, pos) and spawned < count then
          spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
          spawned = spawned + 1
        end
      end
    else
      local y = random(min_y, max_y)
      local start_x = random(min_x, max_x - 2)
      for dx = 0, 2 do
        local pos = {x = start_x + dx, y = y}
        if is_position_available(s, pos) and spawned < count then
          spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
          spawned = spawned + 1
        end
      end
    end

    attempts = attempts + 1
  end
end

-- Fisher-Yates, mirrors Godot Array.shuffle.
local function shuffle(t)
  for i = #t, 2, -1 do
    local j = random(1, i)
    t[i], t[j] = t[j], t[i]
  end
end

local function spawn_corner_shields(s, count, _avoid_edges)
  local spawned = 0
  local attempts = 0
  local max_attempts = count * 10

  local corner_zones = {
    -- Top-left
    {{x = 1, y = 1}, {x = 2, y = 1}, {x = 1, y = 2}, {x = 2, y = 2}},
    -- Top-right
    {{x = CELLS_X - 2, y = 1}, {x = CELLS_X - 3, y = 1}, {x = CELLS_X - 2, y = 2}, {x = CELLS_X - 3, y = 2}},
    -- Bottom-left
    {{x = 1, y = CELLS_Y - 2}, {x = 2, y = CELLS_Y - 2}, {x = 1, y = CELLS_Y - 3}, {x = 2, y = CELLS_Y - 3}},
    -- Bottom-right
    {{x = CELLS_X - 2, y = CELLS_Y - 2}, {x = CELLS_X - 3, y = CELLS_Y - 2}, {x = CELLS_X - 2, y = CELLS_Y - 3}, {x = CELLS_X - 3, y = CELLS_Y - 3}},
  }

  local obstacles_per_corner = math.max(1, math.floor(count / 4))
  for _, corner_positions in ipairs(corner_zones) do
    local corner_spawned = 0
    shuffle(corner_positions)

    for _, pos in ipairs(corner_positions) do
      if spawned >= count then break end
      if corner_spawned >= obstacles_per_corner then break end

      if is_position_available(s, pos) then
        spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
        spawned = spawned + 1
        corner_spawned = corner_spawned + 1
      end
    end

    attempts = attempts + 1
    if attempts > max_attempts then break end
  end
end

local function spawn_line_barriers(s, count, orientation)
  local spawned = 0

  if orientation == "horizontal" or orientation == "both" then
    local num_lines = (count <= 6) and 1 or 2
    for _ = 1, num_lines do
      local y = random(2, CELLS_Y - 3)
      if y >= 3 and y <= 9 then  -- Avoid player/snake zone
        y = random(10, CELLS_Y - 3)
      end

      local line_start_x = random(1, 3)
      local line_end_x = random(CELLS_X - 4, CELLS_X - 2)
      local gap_position = randr(line_start_x + 2, line_end_x - 2)

      for x = line_start_x, line_end_x do
        if spawned >= count then break end
        if math.abs(x - gap_position) <= 1 then
          -- skip gap
        else
          local pos = {x = x, y = y}
          if is_position_available(s, pos) then
            spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
            spawned = spawned + 1
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  if orientation == "vertical" or orientation == "both" then
    local num_lines = (count <= 6) and 1 or 2
    for _ = 1, num_lines do
      local x = random(2, CELLS_X - 3)

      local line_start_y = random(1, 3)
      local line_end_y = random(CELLS_Y - 4, CELLS_Y - 2)
      local gap_position = randr(line_start_y + 2, line_end_y - 2)

      for y = line_start_y, line_end_y do
        if spawned >= count then break end
        if math.abs(y - gap_position) <= 1 then
          -- skip gap
        else
          local pos = {x = x, y = y}
          if is_position_available(s, pos) then
            spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
            spawned = spawned + 1
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

local function spawn_bunker_obstacles(s, count, bunker_type)
  local spawned = 0
  local attempts = 0
  local max_attempts = count * 10

  local obstacles_per_bunker = (bunker_type == "L") and 3 or 4
  local num_bunkers = math.max(1, math.floor(count / obstacles_per_bunker))

  -- Polish fix vs. the Godot original: retry a fresh center when the chosen one
  -- is too close to a start, instead of burning the bunker slot. The original
  -- `continue` advanced the bunker counter, so low-count bunker levels (4, 10)
  -- could place ZERO cover. Here a bunker slot is only consumed once it places.
  local bunkers_placed = 0
  while bunkers_placed < num_bunkers and spawned < count and attempts < max_attempts do
    attempts = attempts + 1

    local center_pos = {x = random(2, CELLS_X - 3), y = random(2, CELLS_Y - 3)}
    if dist(center_pos, s.player_start) < 3 or dist(center_pos, s.snake_start) < 3 then
      -- too close; try another center
    else
      local rotation = random(0, 3)
      local bunker_positions

      if bunker_type == "L" then
        if rotation == 0 then
          bunker_positions = {{x = 0, y = 0}, {x = 1, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = 1}}
        elseif rotation == 1 then
          bunker_positions = {{x = 0, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = 1}, {x = -1, y = 1}}
        elseif rotation == 2 then
          bunker_positions = {{x = 0, y = 0}, {x = -1, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = -1}}
        else
          bunker_positions = {{x = 0, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = -1}, {x = 1, y = -1}}
        end
      else  -- T-shape
        if rotation == 0 then
          bunker_positions = {{x = -1, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = 0}, {x = 1, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = 1}}
        elseif rotation == 1 then
          bunker_positions = {{x = 0, y = -1}, {x = 0, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = 1}, {x = -1, y = 0}}
        elseif rotation == 2 then
          bunker_positions = {{x = -1, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = 0}, {x = 1, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = -1}}
        else
          bunker_positions = {{x = 0, y = -1}, {x = 0, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = 1}, {x = 1, y = 0}}
        end
      end

      local placed_any = false
      for _, offset in ipairs(bunker_positions) do
        if spawned >= count then break end
        local pos = {x = center_pos.x + offset.x, y = center_pos.y + offset.y}
        if is_position_available(s, pos) then
          spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
          spawned = spawned + 1
          placed_any = true
        end
      end
      if placed_any then bunkers_placed = bunkers_placed + 1 end
    end
  end
end

local function spawn_symmetrical_obstacles(s, count, axis)
  local spawned = 0
  local attempts = 0
  local max_attempts = count * 10

  while spawned < count and attempts < max_attempts do
    local base_x = random(1, CELLS_X - 2)
    local base_y = random(1, CELLS_Y - 2)
    local base_pos = {x = base_x, y = base_y}

    local skip = false
    if dist(base_pos, s.player_start) < 2 or dist(base_pos, s.snake_start) < 2 then
      attempts = attempts + 1
      skip = true
    elseif not is_position_available(s, base_pos) then
      attempts = attempts + 1
      skip = true
    end

    if not skip then
      local positions_to_spawn = {base_pos}

      if axis == "horizontal" or axis == "both" then
        local center_x = CELLS_X / 2.0
        local mirror_x = math.floor(2 * center_x - base_x)
        if mirror_x >= 0 and mirror_x < CELLS_X then
          local mirror_pos = {x = mirror_x, y = base_y}
          if not (mirror_pos.x == base_pos.x and mirror_pos.y == base_pos.y) then
            positions_to_spawn[#positions_to_spawn + 1] = mirror_pos
          end
        end
      end

      if axis == "vertical" or axis == "both" then
        local center_y = CELLS_Y / 2.0
        local mirror_y = math.floor(2 * center_y - base_y)
        if mirror_y >= 0 and mirror_y < CELLS_Y then
          local mirror_pos = {x = base_x, y = mirror_y}
          if not (mirror_pos.x == base_pos.x and mirror_pos.y == base_pos.y) then
            positions_to_spawn[#positions_to_spawn + 1] = mirror_pos
          end
        end
      end

      if axis == "both" then
        local center_x = CELLS_X / 2.0
        local center_y = CELLS_Y / 2.0
        local mirror_x = math.floor(2 * center_x - base_x)
        local mirror_y = math.floor(2 * center_y - base_y)
        if mirror_x >= 0 and mirror_x < CELLS_X and mirror_y >= 0 and mirror_y < CELLS_Y then
          local diagonal_mirror = {x = mirror_x, y = mirror_y}
          local exists = false
          for _, p in ipairs(positions_to_spawn) do
            if p.x == diagonal_mirror.x and p.y == diagonal_mirror.y then
              exists = true
              break
            end
          end
          if not exists then
            positions_to_spawn[#positions_to_spawn + 1] = diagonal_mirror
          end
        end
      end

      local all_available = true
      for _, pos in ipairs(positions_to_spawn) do
        if not is_position_available(s, pos) then
          all_available = false
          break
        end
      end

      if all_available then
        for _, pos in ipairs(positions_to_spawn) do
          if spawned < count then
            spawn_obstacle_at(s, pos)
            spawned = spawned + 1
          end
        end
      end

      attempts = attempts + 1
    end
  end
end

-- ============ PUBLIC API ============

-- generate_obstacles_for_level (main.gd 347-401) + dispatch.
-- Returns an array of {x=,y=} obstacle cells.
function M.generate(level, player_start, snake_start, rng)
  random = rng.random
  player_start = player_start or {x = C.PLAYER_START_X, y = C.PLAYER_START_Y}
  snake_start = snake_start or {x = C.SNAKE_START_X, y = C.SNAKE_START_Y}

  local s = new_state(player_start, snake_start)

  local cfg = config.get_config_for_level(level)
  local count = cfg.count or 0

  -- Randomization: +/-2 from base, clamped to [3,7].
  if cfg.randomize then
    local random_offset = random(-2, 2)
    count = count + random_offset
    if count < 3 then count = 3 end
    if count > 7 then count = 7 end
  end

  if count <= 0 then
    return s.positions
  end

  local pattern = cfg.pattern or "random"
  local avoid_edges = cfg.avoid_edges
  if avoid_edges == nil then avoid_edges = true end
  local cluster_size = cfg.cluster_size or 1

  if pattern == "random" then
    spawn_random_obstacles(s, count, avoid_edges)
  elseif pattern == "scattered" then
    spawn_scattered_obstacles(s, count, avoid_edges, cluster_size)
  elseif pattern == "center" then
    spawn_center_obstacles(s, count, avoid_edges)
  elseif pattern == "perimeter" then
    spawn_perimeter_obstacles(s, count)
  elseif pattern == "maze" then
    spawn_maze_obstacles(s, count, avoid_edges)
  elseif pattern == "corner_shields" then
    spawn_corner_shields(s, count, avoid_edges)
  elseif pattern == "line_barriers" then
    local orientation = cfg.orientation or "horizontal"
    spawn_line_barriers(s, count, orientation)
  elseif pattern == "bunkers" then
    local bunker_type = cfg.bunker_type or "L"
    spawn_bunker_obstacles(s, count, bunker_type)
  elseif pattern == "symmetrical" then
    local axis = cfg.axis or "horizontal"
    spawn_symmetrical_obstacles(s, count, axis)
  else
    spawn_random_obstacles(s, count, avoid_edges)
  end

  return s.positions
end

return M

-- Seeded generator for gameplay randomness. Ranked runs replay on the server,
-- so gameplay must never call math.random; presentation may.
-- random() / random(m) / random(m, n) follow Lua's math.random conventions.
local M = {}

function M.new(seed)
	local self = { state = math.floor(tonumber(seed) or 1) % 2147483647 }
	if self.state <= 0 then self.state = self.state + 2147483646 end

	function self.random(m, n)
		self.state = (self.state * 48271) % 2147483647
		local r = (self.state - 1) / 2147483646
		if m == nil then return r end
		if n == nil then m, n = 1, m end
		return m + math.floor(r * (n - m + 1))
	end

	return self
end

-- Rebuilds a generator from a saved state (see sim.save).
function M.restore(state)
	local g = M.new(1)
	g.state = state
	return g
end

return M

-- Sneak gameplay, free of engine calls so the Scoreosis verifier can replay it.
-- Functions take the game state table `s`: the controller passes its own
-- instance (presentation fields live beside these), the verifier a plain table.
-- Time advances only through M.tick, one 1/60 s step; player actions apply at
-- the start of a tick. Presentation reads s.events after each call.
local C = require "script.game_config"
local grid = require "script.grid"
local ai = require "script.ai"
local vision = require "script.vision"
local obstacles = require "script.obstacles"
local difficulty = require "script.difficulty"
local snake_config = require "script.snake_config"
local rng = require "script.rng"

local M = {}

M.DT = 1 / 60
-- Seconds a destructible cover block must "rest" between hides: after you hide beside
-- it (crack), it can't take the breaking second hide until this elapses AND you re-approach.
M.DESTRUCT_COOLDOWN = 1.2
M.OBSTACLE_MOVE_INTERVAL = 0.55
M.STUN_TIME = 1.0

local STRIKE_DIRS = { { x = 0, y = -1 }, { x = 0, y = 1 }, { x = -1, y = 0 }, { x = 1, y = 0 } }
M.STRIKE_DIRS = STRIKE_DIRS

local function emit(s, kind, data)
  data = data or {}
  data.kind = kind
  s.events[#s.events + 1] = data
end

local function sfx(s, name)
  emit(s, "sfx", { name = name })
end

-- Presentation feedback cue (chips, haptics, shake) at a cell.
local function fx(s, name, x, y)
  emit(s, "fx", { name = name, x = x, y = y })
end

function M.is_obstacle(s, x, y)
  return s.obstacle_set ~= nil and s.obstacle_set[x * 1000 + y] ~= nil
end

function M.is_spike(s, x, y)
  local ob = s.obstacle_set and s.obstacle_set[x * 1000 + y]
  return type(ob) == "table" and ob.type == "spike"
end

-- ---------- level construction ----------

function M.clear_snake(s)
  s.snake_data = {}
  emit(s, "snake_cleared")
end

function M.clear_obstacles(s)
  s.obstacle_list = {}
  s.obstacle_set = {}
  s.movers = {}
  s.mover_accum = 0
  s.destructibles = {}
end

-- Tier-1 dynamic obstacles (panel-approved). From L4 a share of bricks become
-- DESTRUCTIBLE (smash to open a lane); from L6 a couple become MOVING (a fixed
-- 2-cell rail shuttle that shifts cover). Static bricks stay the majority every
-- board: dynamic types are capped at 40% of the obstacle count, ramped slowly.
local function assign_obstacle_types(s, cells)
  local random = s.rng.random
  local total = #cells
  local types = {}
  if total == 0 then return types end
  local occ = {}
  for _, c in ipairs(cells) do occ[c.x * 1000 + c.y] = true end
  local ps = { x = C.PLAYER_START_X, y = C.PLAYER_START_Y }
  local ss = { x = C.SNAKE_START_X, y = C.SNAKE_START_Y }
  local function rail_ok(x, y)
    if x < 0 or x >= C.CELLS_X or y < 0 or y >= C.CELLS_Y then return false end
    if occ[x * 1000 + y] then return false end
    if math.abs(x - ps.x) + math.abs(y - ps.y) < 3 then return false end
    if math.abs(x - ss.x) + math.abs(y - ss.y) < 3 then return false end
    return true
  end
  local max_dyn = math.floor(total * 0.4)
  local order = {}
  for i = 1, total do order[i] = i end
  for i = total, 2, -1 do local j = random(i); order[i], order[j] = order[j], order[i] end

  -- Spikes get first pick of the dynamic budget (rarest, highest-level hazard:
  -- lethal to the player, baitable by the snake). Only on open cells (>=3 free
  -- neighbours) and well clear of spawns, so they never wall off the only path.
  local function open_enough(x, y)
    local free = 0
    for _, d in ipairs({ { 1, 0 }, { -1, 0 }, { 0, 1 }, { 0, -1 } }) do
      local ax, ay = x + d[1], y + d[2]
      if ax >= 0 and ax < C.CELLS_X and ay >= 0 and ay < C.CELLS_Y and not occ[ax * 1000 + ay] then
        free = free + 1
      end
    end
    return free >= 3
  end
  local n_spike = (s.level >= 9) and math.min(1 + math.floor((s.level - 9) / 4), 2) or 0
  n_spike = math.min(n_spike, max_dyn)
  local sp = 0
  for _, idx in ipairs(order) do
    if sp >= n_spike then break end
    local c = cells[idx]
    if math.abs(c.x - ps.x) + math.abs(c.y - ps.y) >= 4
      and math.abs(c.x - ss.x) + math.abs(c.y - ss.y) >= 3
      and open_enough(c.x, c.y) then
      types[idx] = { type = "spike" }
      sp = sp + 1
    end
  end

  -- Movers next: a fixed 2-cell rail shuttle (needs a free adjacent rail cell).
  local n_move = (s.level >= 6) and math.min(1 + math.floor((s.level - 6) / 4), 3) or 0
  n_move = math.min(n_move, math.max(0, max_dyn - sp))
  local moved = 0
  for _, idx in ipairs(order) do
    if moved >= n_move then break end
    if not types[idx] then
      local c = cells[idx]
      local dirs = { { 1, 0 }, { -1, 0 }, { 0, 1 }, { 0, -1 } }
      for i = #dirs, 2, -1 do local j = random(i); dirs[i], dirs[j] = dirs[j], dirs[i] end
      for _, d in ipairs(dirs) do
        local bx, by = c.x + d[1], c.y + d[2]
        if rail_ok(bx, by) then
          local rail = (d[1] ~= 0)
            and { axis = "h", lo = math.min(c.x, bx), hi = math.max(c.x, bx), dir = d[1] }
            or { axis = "v", lo = math.min(c.y, by), hi = math.max(c.y, by), dir = d[2] }
          types[idx] = { type = "moving", rail = rail }
          occ[bx * 1000 + by] = true       -- reserve the rail's empty cell
          moved = moved + 1
          break
        end
      end
    end
  end

  -- Destructibles fill whatever dynamic budget is left.
  local n_destruct = (s.level >= 4) and math.max(1, math.floor(total * 0.3)) or 0
  n_destruct = math.min(n_destruct, math.max(0, max_dyn - sp - moved))
  local dn = 0
  for _, idx in ipairs(order) do
    if dn >= n_destruct then break end
    if not types[idx] then types[idx] = { type = "destructible" }; dn = dn + 1 end
  end
  return types
end

-- Rebuilds the lookup tables from s.obstacle_list (also used after loading a save).
function M.index_obstacles(s)
  s.obstacle_set, s.movers, s.destructibles = {}, {}, {}
  for _, ob in ipairs(s.obstacle_list) do
    s.obstacle_set[ob.x * 1000 + ob.y] = ob
    if ob.type == "moving" then table.insert(s.movers, ob) end
    if ob.type == "destructible" then table.insert(s.destructibles, ob) end
  end
end

local function generate_obstacles(s)
  M.clear_obstacles(s)
  local cells = obstacles.generate(s.level,
    { x = C.PLAYER_START_X, y = C.PLAYER_START_Y },
    { x = C.SNAKE_START_X, y = C.SNAKE_START_Y }, s.rng)
  local types = assign_obstacle_types(s, cells)
  s.next_obstacle_id = s.next_obstacle_id or 0
  for i, c in ipairs(cells) do
    local t = types[i] or { type = "brick" }
    s.next_obstacle_id = s.next_obstacle_id + 1
    table.insert(s.obstacle_list, {
      id = s.next_obstacle_id, type = t.type, x = c.x, y = c.y, rail = t.rail, stage = 0, cd = 0,
    })
  end
  M.index_obstacles(s)
  emit(s, "obstacles_reset")
end

function M.add_segment(s, pos)
  table.insert(s.snake_data, { x = pos.x, y = pos.y })
end

local function calc_snake_length(s, level)
  local cfg = s.snake_cfg
  local bonus = difficulty.units(level) * cfg.length_growth
  local rf = 0.8 + s.rng.random() * 0.4          -- ±20%
  local len = cfg.base_length + math.floor(bonus * rf)
  len = math.min(len, math.min(10, C.CELLS_Y - 5))
  return math.max(len, 2)
end

-- Derived from snake_type + the level; also rebuilt after loading a save.
function M.apply_snake_type(s)
  s.snake_cfg = snake_config.get_type(s.snake_type)
end

local function load_level_config(s, level)
  local selected, cfg = snake_config.select_snake_for_level(level, s.rng)
  s.snake_type = selected
  M.apply_snake_type(s)
  local range_mult = cfg.range_multiplier or 1.0
  if cfg.random_range then
    range_mult = range_mult * (cfg.range_min + s.rng.random() * (cfg.range_max - cfg.range_min))
  end
  s.vision_range = s.snake_cfg.vision_range * range_mult
  s.food_threshold = s.snake_cfg.food_threshold
  local sm = s.snake_cfg.speed_multiplier
  local mult = sm[s.rng.random(#sm)]
  s.snake_speed = (C.BASE_SNAKE_SPEED + difficulty.units(level) * C.SNAKE_SPEED_INCREMENT) * mult
  s.move_interval = math.max(C.MOVE_INTERVAL_MIN, C.MOVE_INTERVAL / s.snake_speed)
  -- Gentle on-ramp: the green snake is the fast one, so the first levels feel
  -- rushed to a new player. Slow levels 1-2 so they can learn bait + strike.
  if level == 1 then s.move_interval = s.move_interval * 1.5
  elseif level == 2 then s.move_interval = s.move_interval * 1.25 end
end

-- A column (x, y..y+n-1) is a legal snake spawn only if every cell is on-grid,
-- clear of the player, and clear of obstacles (obstacles are generated first).
local function column_clear(s, x, y, n)
  for i = 0, n - 1 do
    local cy = y + i
    if x == s.player_pos.x and cy == s.player_pos.y then return false end
    if s.obstacle_set and s.obstacle_set[x * 1000 + cy] then return false end
  end
  return true
end

-- Pick a head row that keeps the whole downward body on-grid (y in [0, CELLS_Y-n]),
-- >=5 cells from the player, and off every obstacle. Random first, then a
-- deterministic scan so we never fall back onto an occupied column.
local function find_safe_spawn(s, n)
  local maxy = math.max(0, C.CELLS_Y - n)
  for _ = 1, 60 do
    local x = s.rng.random(2, C.CELLS_X - 3)
    local y = s.rng.random(0, maxy)
    if math.abs(x - s.player_pos.x) + math.abs(y - s.player_pos.y) >= 5
      and column_clear(s, x, y, n) then
      return { x = x, y = y }
    end
  end
  for x = 0, C.CELLS_X - 1 do
    for y = 0, maxy do
      if column_clear(s, x, y, n) then return { x = x, y = y } end
    end
  end
  return { x = C.CELLS_X - 3, y = maxy }
end

M.find_safe_spawn = find_safe_spawn

local function spawn_snake(s, pos, n)
  pos = pos or { x = C.SNAKE_START_X, y = C.SNAKE_START_Y }
  n = n or calc_snake_length(s, s.level)
  -- clamp so the downward-built body stays on-grid (safety net)
  local sy = math.max(0, math.min(pos.y, C.CELLS_Y - n))
  s.snake_facing = { x = 0, y = -1 }
  for i = 0, n - 1 do
    M.add_segment(s, { x = pos.x, y = sy + i })
  end
end

local function food_cell_free(s, x, y)
  if x == s.player_pos.x and y == s.player_pos.y then return false end
  if s.obstacle_set and s.obstacle_set[x * 1000 + y] then return false end
  for _, seg in ipairs(s.snake_data) do
    if seg.x == x and seg.y == y then return false end
  end
  return true
end

function M.move_food(s)
  -- Random first, then a deterministic scan, so a crowded board (the snake grows as
  -- it eats) can never spin the old uncapped rejection loop forever.
  local fx_, fy
  for _ = 1, 200 do
    local x, y = s.rng.random(0, C.CELLS_X - 1), s.rng.random(0, C.CELLS_Y - 1)
    if food_cell_free(s, x, y) then fx_, fy = x, y; break end
  end
  if not fx_ then
    for y = 0, C.CELLS_Y - 1 do
      for x = 0, C.CELLS_X - 1 do
        if food_cell_free(s, x, y) then fx_, fy = x, y; break end
      end
      if fx_ then break end
    end
  end
  fx_ = fx_ or s.player_pos.x
  fy = fy or s.player_pos.y
  s.food_pos = { x = fx_, y = fy }
  emit(s, "food_moved", { x = fx_, y = fy })
end

local function reset_level_flags(s)
  s.stuck = 0
  s.chasing = false
  s.lost_timer = 0
  s.last_known = nil
  s.move_accum = 0
  s.level_transition = 0
  s.snake_stunned = false
  s.snake_invulnerable = false
  s.stun_timer = 0
  s.invuln_timer = 0
  s.food_destroyed = 0
  s.level_food_score = 0
  s.level_chop_score = 0
  s.level_pursued = false
  s.level_chopped = false
end

function M.new_facts()
  return {
    cleared = 0, clears = 0, chops = 0, food = 0,
    spike_baits = 0, covers = 0, silent_clears = 0, food_only_clears = 0,
  }
end

-- Every field of the ranked state; save/load copy exactly these.
local SAVED = {
  "score", "level", "game_over", "death_cause", "started", "snake_data", "stuck", "chasing",
  "lost_timer", "last_known", "move_accum", "level_transition", "snake_stunned",
  "snake_invulnerable", "stun_timer", "invuln_timer", "food_destroyed", "level_food_score",
  "level_chop_score", "level_pursued", "level_chopped", "snake_type", "vision_range",
  "food_threshold", "snake_speed", "move_interval", "obstacle_list", "mover_accum",
  "next_obstacle_id", "player_pos", "facing", "snake_facing", "food_pos", "facts",
}

-- Starts a fresh run on `s` from `seed`. `s` may be a reused table (the
-- controller), so every saved field restarts from nil like a fresh one.
function M.new_game(s, seed)
  for _, key in ipairs(SAVED) do s[key] = nil end
  s.events = {}
  s.rng = rng.new(seed)
  s.score = 0
  s.level = 1
  s.game_over = false
  s.death_cause = nil
  s.started = false
  s.snake_data = {}
  s.facts = M.new_facts()
  reset_level_flags(s)
  load_level_config(s, s.level)
  generate_obstacles(s)
  s.player_pos = { x = C.PLAYER_START_X, y = C.PLAYER_START_Y }
  s.facing = { x = 0, y = -1 }
  -- Spawn via find_safe_spawn (not the fixed start) so a segment never overlaps an
  -- obstacle: obstacle gen only clears dist<2 of SNAKE_START, but a 3-cell body
  -- reaches dist 2 (e.g. (4,10)), which a brick may legally occupy.
  local n = calc_snake_length(s, s.level)
  spawn_snake(s, find_safe_spawn(s, n), n)
  M.move_food(s)
  emit(s, "level_started", { level = s.level })
end

local function spawn_next_level(s)
  M.clear_snake(s)
  load_level_config(s, s.level)
  generate_obstacles(s)
  local n = calc_snake_length(s, s.level)
  spawn_snake(s, find_safe_spawn(s, n), n)
  M.move_food(s)
  reset_level_flags(s)
  emit(s, "level_started", { level = s.level })
end
M.spawn_next_level = spawn_next_level

-- `cause` is "food", "chop", "stuck" or "spike": what took the last segment.
local function kill_snake_advance(s, cause)
  local last = s.snake_data[1]
  local f = s.facts
  f.cleared = math.max(f.cleared, s.level)
  f.clears = f.clears + 1
  if not s.level_pursued then f.silent_clears = f.silent_clears + 1 end
  if cause == "food" and not s.level_chopped then f.food_only_clears = f.food_only_clears + 1 end
  M.clear_snake(s)
  s.score = s.score + C.CLEAR_BONUS * s.level
  s.level = s.level + 1
  s.level_transition = C.LEVEL_TRANSITION_DELAY
  sfx(s, "sfx_level")
  fx(s, "clear", last and last.x, last and last.y)
  emit(s, "level_cleared", { level = s.level - 1 })
end

-- ---------- vision ----------

local function can_see_player(s, head)
  return vision.can_see(head, s.player_pos, s.snake_facing,
    s.vision_range, s.snake_cfg.vision_width, s.snake_cfg.vision_type,
    function(x, y) return M.is_obstacle(s, x, y) end, s.food_pos)
end

-- ---------- attack / damage ----------

local function pop_tail(s)
  local tail = table.remove(s.snake_data)
  if tail then emit(s, "tail_popped", { x = tail.x, y = tail.y }) end
end

local function damage_snake_from_food(s)
  if #s.snake_data <= 1 then
    kill_snake_advance(s, "food")
    return
  end
  pop_tail(s)
end

-- Entering player pursuit (sight or a hit): the alert marker shows once.
-- Staying in pursuit never replays it; a stunned snake gets none.
local function enter_pursuit(s)
  local entering = not s.chasing
  s.chasing = true
  s.level_pursued = true
  s.lost_timer = C.SNAKE_LOST_PLAYER_DURATION
  if entering and not s.snake_stunned and s.snake_data[1] then
    sfx(s, "sfx_alert")
    emit(s, "alert")
  end
end

local function attack_snake(s)
  if #s.snake_data == 0 or s.snake_invulnerable then return end
  sfx(s, "sfx_snake_hit")
  s.facts.chops = s.facts.chops + 1
  s.level_chopped = true
  if (s.level_chop_score or 0) < C.CHOP_SCORE_CAP then
    s.score = s.score + C.ATTACK_SCORE_MULTIPLIER * s.level
    s.level_chop_score = (s.level_chop_score or 0) + 1
  end
  s.snake_invulnerable = true
  s.invuln_timer = math.min(s.level, C.INVULN_MAX)
  -- React to being hit: look toward the attacker and remember where they are as
  -- the last-known spot, then go hunt it (see snake_tick). Natural "what hit me?"
  local head = s.snake_data[1]
  local dx = s.player_pos.x - head.x
  local dy = s.player_pos.y - head.y
  if math.abs(dx) >= math.abs(dy) then
    if dx ~= 0 then s.snake_facing = (dx > 0) and { x = 1, y = 0 } or { x = -1, y = 0 } end
  else
    s.snake_facing = (dy > 0) and { x = 0, y = 1 } or { x = 0, y = -1 }
  end
  s.last_known = { x = s.player_pos.x, y = s.player_pos.y }
  if #s.snake_data == 1 then
    s.chasing = true
    s.level_pursued = true
    s.lost_timer = C.SNAKE_LOST_PLAYER_DURATION
    kill_snake_advance(s, "chop")
    return
  end
  s.snake_stunned = true
  s.stun_timer = M.STUN_TIME
  emit(s, "stunned")
  enter_pursuit(s)
  local tail = s.snake_data[#s.snake_data]
  pop_tail(s)
  fx(s, "segment", tail.x, tail.y)
end

local function segment_at(s, x, y)
  for i = 1, #s.snake_data do
    if s.snake_data[i].x == x and s.snake_data[i].y == y then return true end
  end
  return false
end

-- Strike targeting (shared by every scheme so none is easier). You point a direction;
-- it hits that cell if it holds a segment, else auto-targets the nearest adjacent
-- segment to that direction. Food is deliberate: only the pointed-at cell.
function M.pick_strike_cell(s, dir)
  local ax, ay = s.player_pos.x + dir.x, s.player_pos.y + dir.y
  if grid.in_bounds(ax, ay) and segment_at(s, ax, ay) then return ax, ay end
  local best, bx, by
  for _, d in ipairs(STRIKE_DIRS) do
    local cx, cy = s.player_pos.x + d.x, s.player_pos.y + d.y
    if grid.in_bounds(cx, cy) and segment_at(s, cx, cy) then
      local align = d.x * dir.x + d.y * dir.y   -- prefer the segment nearest the pointed direction
      if not best or align > best then best = align; bx, by = cx, cy end
    end
  end
  return bx, by
end

function M.player_death(s, cause)
  if s.game_over then return end
  s.game_over = true
  s.death_cause = cause
  emit(s, "death", { cause = cause, x = s.player_pos.x, y = s.player_pos.y })
end

-- Strike toward `dir` (defaults to the current facing = a bare tap / SPACE).
function M.perform_attack(s, dir)
  if s.game_over then return end
  dir = dir or s.facing
  if not s.started then s.started = true end
  local ax, ay = s.player_pos.x + dir.x, s.player_pos.y + dir.y
  local hit_food = grid.in_bounds(ax, ay) and ax == s.food_pos.x and ay == s.food_pos.y
  local bx, by
  if not hit_food then bx, by = M.pick_strike_cell(s, dir) end
  -- face where we actually strike (slash FX + sprite look)
  if bx then s.facing = { x = bx - s.player_pos.x, y = by - s.player_pos.y }
  else s.facing = { x = dir.x, y = dir.y } end
  emit(s, "attack")
  if hit_food then
    sfx(s, "sfx_food_squish")
    s.facts.food = s.facts.food + 1
    local fp = ((s.level_food_score or 0) < C.FOOD_SCORE_CAP) and 1 or 0
    s.score = s.score + fp
    s.level_food_score = (s.level_food_score or 0) + fp
    s.food_destroyed = s.food_destroyed + 1
    if s.food_destroyed >= s.food_threshold and #s.snake_data > 0 then
      s.food_destroyed = 0
      local tail = s.snake_data[#s.snake_data]
      local clears = #s.snake_data <= 1
      damage_snake_from_food(s)
      sfx(s, "sfx_hit")
      if not clears then fx(s, "segment", tail.x, tail.y) end   -- a clear uses its own cue
    else
      sfx(s, "sfx_food")
      fx(s, "food", ax, ay)
    end
    M.move_food(s)
    return
  end
  if bx then
    if s.snake_invulnerable then fx(s, "blocked", bx, by) end
    attack_snake(s)
  else
    fx(s, "miss")
  end
end

-- ---------- player movement ----------

local function manhattan_adj(ax, ay, bx, by)
  return math.abs(ax - bx) + math.abs(ay - by) == 1
end

local function destroy_obstacle(s, ob)
  s.obstacle_set[ob.x * 1000 + ob.y] = nil
  for i, o in ipairs(s.obstacle_list) do
    if o == ob then table.remove(s.obstacle_list, i); break end
  end
  s.facts.covers = s.facts.covers + 1
  sfx(s, "sfx_brick_break")
  fx(s, "break", ob.x, ob.y)
  emit(s, "obstacle_removed", { id = ob.id })
end

-- Destructible cover degrades when the player HIDES beside it (a fresh approach: stepping
-- into a cell adjacent to it FROM a non-adjacent cell). 1st hide cracks it (telegraph); the
-- 2nd hide -- only after its cooldown, and only on another fresh approach -- crumbles it and
-- opens the lane. Player-only.
local function check_hide(s, ox, oy, nx, ny)
  if not s.destructibles then return end
  for i = #s.destructibles, 1, -1 do
    local d = s.destructibles[i]
    local approaching = manhattan_adj(nx, ny, d.x, d.y) and not manhattan_adj(ox, oy, d.x, d.y)
    if approaching and (d.cd or 0) <= 0 then
      if (d.stage or 0) == 0 then
        d.stage = 1
        d.cd = M.DESTRUCT_COOLDOWN
        sfx(s, "sfx_brick_creak")
        fx(s, "crack", d.x, d.y)
        emit(s, "obstacle_cracked", { id = d.id })
      else
        table.remove(s.destructibles, i)
        destroy_obstacle(s, d)        -- crumbles: shard burst + sfx + opens the lane
      end
    end
  end
end

function M.try_move(s, dx, dy)
  if s.game_over then return end
  s.facing = { x = dx, y = dy }
  if not s.started then s.started = true end
  local ox, oy = s.player_pos.x, s.player_pos.y
  local nx, ny = ox + dx, oy + dy
  if not grid.in_bounds(nx, ny) then return end
  -- moving into the snake is death (without overlapping)
  for _, seg in ipairs(s.snake_data) do
    if nx == seg.x and ny == seg.y then M.player_death(s, "snake") return end
  end
  -- food blocks; spikes are lethal; bricks, destructibles and movers all just block movement
  if nx == s.food_pos.x and ny == s.food_pos.y then return end
  local ob = s.obstacle_set[nx * 1000 + ny]
  if ob then
    if type(ob) == "table" and ob.type == "spike" then M.player_death(s, "spike") end
    return
  end
  sfx(s, "sfx_step_ninja")
  s.player_pos.x, s.player_pos.y = nx, ny
  emit(s, "player_moved")
  check_hide(s, ox, oy, nx, ny)       -- degrade any destructible cover we just hid beside
end

-- ---------- snake tick ----------

local function snake_tick(s)
  if s.snake_stunned or #s.snake_data == 0 then return end
  local old = {}
  for i = 1, #s.snake_data do old[i] = { x = s.snake_data[i].x, y = s.snake_data[i].y } end

  local head = s.snake_data[1]
  local sd = s.snake_data
  local function valid_fn(x, y)
    if x < 0 or x >= C.CELLS_X or y < 0 or y >= C.CELLS_Y then return false end
    for i = 2, #sd do
      if sd[i].x == x and sd[i].y == y then return false end
    end
    -- spikes are passable ONLY while the snake is actively chasing, so the player
    -- can bait it across one (it can't reach a spike when idly seeking food)
    if M.is_obstacle(s, x, y) and not (s.chasing and M.is_spike(s, x, y)) then return false end
    return true
  end

  -- Targeting: if it can see you, hunt your live position and remember it as the
  -- LAST-KNOWN spot. If it loses sight but is still alert, walk to that spot to
  -- search; on reaching it (or when the alert timer expires) it gives up and
  -- goes back to food. Seeing you always overrides food-seeking.
  local see = can_see_player(s, head)
  local target
  if see then
    enter_pursuit(s)
    s.last_known = { x = s.player_pos.x, y = s.player_pos.y }
    target = s.player_pos
  elseif s.chasing and s.last_known then
    if head.x == s.last_known.x and head.y == s.last_known.y then
      s.chasing = false
      s.last_known = nil
      target = s.food_pos
    else
      target = s.last_known
    end
  else
    target = s.food_pos
  end
  -- trap-aware step: pursues the target but won't blunder into a dead-end (see ai.lua).
  -- nil = genuinely boxed in -> count toward the stuck-death (a player-cornered win).
  local move_dir = ai.choose_move(head, target, s.snake_facing, valid_fn)
  if not move_dir then
    s.stuck = s.stuck + 1
    if s.stuck >= C.SNAKE_STUCK_THRESHOLD then
      s.stuck = 0
      kill_snake_advance(s, "stuck")
    end
    return
  end

  s.stuck = 0
  s.snake_data[1] = { x = head.x + move_dir.x, y = head.y + move_dir.y }
  s.snake_facing = move_dir
  for i = 2, #s.snake_data do
    s.snake_data[i] = old[i - 1]
  end

  -- revert if head out of bounds
  local h = s.snake_data[1]
  if h.x < 0 or h.x >= C.CELLS_X or h.y < 0 or h.y >= C.CELLS_Y then
    s.snake_data = old
  end
  -- revert if self-collision
  for i = 2, #s.snake_data do
    if s.snake_data[1].x == s.snake_data[i].x and s.snake_data[1].y == s.snake_data[i].y then
      s.snake_data = old
      break
    end
  end
  if s.snake_data[1].x ~= head.x or s.snake_data[1].y ~= head.y then sfx(s, "sfx_step_snake") end
  emit(s, "snake_moved")
  -- snake eats food: grow by old tail, respawn food
  if #s.snake_data > 0 and s.snake_data[1].x == s.food_pos.x and s.snake_data[1].y == s.food_pos.y then
    M.add_segment(s, old[#old])
    local h2 = s.snake_data[1]
    fx(s, "eat", h2.x, h2.y)
    M.move_food(s)
    sfx(s, "sfx_snake_chomp")
  end
  -- snake stepped onto a spike (only reachable while chasing): a bite of damage +
  -- stun + recoil, no score. This is the bait reward -- lure it across a spike.
  local sh = s.snake_data[1]
  if sh and M.is_spike(s, sh.x, sh.y) then
    sfx(s, "sfx_hit")
    s.facts.spike_baits = s.facts.spike_baits + 1
    if #s.snake_data <= 1 then kill_snake_advance(s, "spike"); return end
    local tail = s.snake_data[#s.snake_data]
    s.snake_stunned = true
    s.stun_timer = M.STUN_TIME
    emit(s, "stunned")
    s.snake_facing = { x = -s.snake_facing.x, y = -s.snake_facing.y }
    pop_tail(s)
    fx(s, "segment", tail.x, tail.y)
  end
  -- player collision = death
  for _, seg in ipairs(s.snake_data) do
    if s.player_pos.x == seg.x and s.player_pos.y == seg.y then
      M.player_death(s, "snake")
      return
    end
  end
end
M.snake_tick = snake_tick

-- A moving obstacle may only step onto an empty board cell (not the player, snake,
-- food, or another obstacle) so it shoves nothing and never crushes the player; if
-- blocked or at a rail end it just reverses. Movers shift the snake's cover/LoS.
local function mover_cell_free(s, x, y)
  if x < 0 or x >= C.CELLS_X or y < 0 or y >= C.CELLS_Y then return false end
  if s.obstacle_set[x * 1000 + y] then return false end
  if s.player_pos and s.player_pos.x == x and s.player_pos.y == y then return false end
  if s.food_pos and s.food_pos.x == x and s.food_pos.y == y then return false end
  for _, seg in ipairs(s.snake_data) do if seg.x == x and seg.y == y then return false end end
  return true
end

local function step_movers(s)
  for _, m in ipairs(s.movers) do
    local nx, ny = m.x, m.y
    if m.rail.axis == "h" then nx = m.x + m.rail.dir else ny = m.y + m.rail.dir end
    local off_rail = (m.rail.axis == "h" and (nx < m.rail.lo or nx > m.rail.hi))
      or (m.rail.axis == "v" and (ny < m.rail.lo or ny > m.rail.hi))
    if off_rail or not mover_cell_free(s, nx, ny) then
      m.rail.dir = -m.rail.dir
    else
      s.obstacle_set[m.x * 1000 + m.y] = nil
      m.x, m.y = nx, ny
      s.obstacle_set[nx * 1000 + ny] = m
      emit(s, "obstacle_moved", { id = m.id })
    end
  end
end

-- ---------- time ----------

-- Advances the game by one fixed 1/60 s step.
function M.tick(s)
  if s.game_over then return end
  local dt = M.DT
  if s.snake_stunned then
    s.stun_timer = s.stun_timer - dt
    if s.stun_timer <= 0 then
      s.snake_stunned = false
      emit(s, "recovered")
    end
  end
  if s.snake_invulnerable then
    s.invuln_timer = s.invuln_timer - dt
    if s.invuln_timer <= 0 then s.snake_invulnerable = false end
  end
  if s.chasing then
    s.lost_timer = s.lost_timer - dt
    if s.lost_timer <= 0 then s.chasing = false; s.last_known = nil; emit(s, "calmed") end
  end
  if s.destructibles then
    for _, d in ipairs(s.destructibles) do
      if (d.cd or 0) > 0 then d.cd = math.max(0, d.cd - dt) end
    end
  end
  if s.level_transition > 0 then
    s.level_transition = s.level_transition - dt
    if s.level_transition <= 0 then spawn_next_level(s) end
    return
  end
  -- Snake waits for the player's first action (faithful game_started gate).
  -- freeze_snake is a presentation-test switch; ranked play never sets it.
  if not s.started or s.freeze_snake then return end
  s.move_accum = s.move_accum + dt
  local ticks = 0
  while s.move_accum >= s.move_interval do
    s.move_accum = s.move_accum - s.move_interval
    snake_tick(s)
    ticks = ticks + 1
    if ticks >= 4 or s.game_over or s.level_transition > 0 or #s.snake_data == 0 then
      if s.move_accum > s.move_interval then s.move_accum = s.move_interval end
      break
    end
  end
  -- dynamic obstacles step on their own fixed, predictable cadence
  if s.movers and #s.movers > 0 then
    s.mover_accum = (s.mover_accum or 0) + dt
    local mt = 0
    while s.mover_accum >= M.OBSTACLE_MOVE_INTERVAL and mt < 4 do
      s.mover_accum = s.mover_accum - M.OBSTACLE_MOVE_INTERVAL
      step_movers(s)
      mt = mt + 1
    end
    if s.mover_accum > M.OBSTACLE_MOVE_INTERVAL then s.mover_accum = M.OBSTACLE_MOVE_INTERVAL end
  end
end

-- ---------- actions ----------

-- One action per tick, encoded for input logs: 0 none, 1-4 move up/down/left/right,
-- 5 strike ahead (auto-target), 6-9 strike up/down/left/right.
M.ACTION_DIRS = { { x = 0, y = -1 }, { x = 0, y = 1 }, { x = -1, y = 0 }, { x = 1, y = 0 } }

function M.apply_action(s, code)
  if code >= 1 and code <= 4 then
    local d = M.ACTION_DIRS[code]
    M.try_move(s, d.x, d.y)
  elseif code == 5 then
    M.perform_attack(s)
  elseif code >= 6 and code <= 9 then
    local d = M.ACTION_DIRS[code - 5]
    M.perform_attack(s, { x = d.x, y = d.y })
  end
end

-- Action code for a move (dx, dy), or a strike when `strike` is set.
function M.action_code(dx, dy, strike)
  for i, d in ipairs(M.ACTION_DIRS) do
    if d.x == dx and d.y == dy then return strike and i + 5 or i end
  end
  return strike and 5 or 0
end

-- ---------- save / load ----------

local function copy(value)
  if type(value) ~= "table" then return value end
  local out = {}
  for k, v in pairs(value) do out[k] = copy(v) end
  return out
end

-- Plain-data snapshot of the gameplay fields (never presentation).
function M.save(s)
  local data = { rng = s.rng.state }
  for _, key in ipairs(SAVED) do data[key] = copy(s[key]) end
  return data
end

-- Restores a snapshot onto `s` (a plain table or the controller instance).
function M.load(s, data)
  for _, key in ipairs(SAVED) do s[key] = copy(data[key]) end
  s.rng = rng.restore(data.rng)
  s.events = {}
  M.apply_snake_type(s)
  M.index_obstacles(s)
  return s
end

return M
modules.script.snake_config:
-- Snake type + per-level configuration, ported from snake_config.gd.
-- Pure data: colours are handled separately (Game Boy mono) in palettes/controller.

local M = {}

  for _, cfg in ipairs(M.level_configurations) do
    if cfg.level == level then return cfg end
  end
  return M.level_configurations[#M.level_configurations]
end

function M.get_type(name)
  return M.types[name] or M.types.green
end

local TIERS = {green = 1, purple = 2, striped = 3, red = 4, blue = 5}

function M.get_tier(name)
  return TIERS[name] or 1
end

function M.get_lower_tier_snakes(tier)
  local lower = {}
  if tier > 1 then lower[#lower + 1] = "green" end
  if tier > 2 then lower[#lower + 1] = "purple" end
  if tier > 3 then lower[#lower + 1] = "striped" end
  if tier > 4 then lower[#lower + 1] = "red" end
  return lower
end

-- Weighted selection: 70% intended snake, 30% a random lower-tier snake.
-- Returns (selected_type, level_config).
function M.select_snake_for_level(level, rng)
  local cfg = M.get_config_for_level(level)
  local intended = cfg.snake_type
  local selected = intended
  if rng.random() > 0.7 then
    local tier = M.get_tier(intended)
    if tier > 1 then
      local lower = M.get_lower_tier_snakes(tier)
      if #lower > 0 then selected = lower[rng.random(#lower)] end
    end
  end
  return selected, cfg
end

return M

-- Pure vision module ported from main.gd (check_*_vision + Bresenham LoS).
-- No engine deps. Cells are {x=,y=}; is_obstacle(x,y) is a predicate.
local C = require "script.game_config"

local M = {}

local function fwd(diff, facing)
  return diff.x * facing.x + diff.y * facing.y
end

-- Cone: narrow at the head, widening to `width` at max range, in front only.
local function cone(diff, facing, range, width)
  local fc = fwd(diff, facing)
  if fc <= 0 or fc > range then return false end
  local wd = 0.5 + (width - 0.5) * (fc / range)
  if facing.x ~= 0 then return math.abs(diff.y) <= wd
  else return math.abs(diff.x) <= wd end
end

-- Rectangle / long-line: fixed width forward (width distinguishes them).
local function fixed_forward(diff, facing, range, width)
  local fc = fwd(diff, facing)
  if fc <= 0 or fc > range then return false end
  if facing.x ~= 0 then return math.abs(diff.y) <= width
  else return math.abs(diff.x) <= width end
end

-- Square: range in all directions.
local function square(diff, _facing, range, _width)
  return math.abs(diff.x) <= range and math.abs(diff.y) <= range
end

-- Cross: only along the 4 cardinals (aligned row/column).
local function cross(diff, _facing, range, _width)
  if math.abs(diff.y) <= 0.5 then return math.abs(diff.x) <= range end
  if math.abs(diff.x) <= 0.5 then return math.abs(diff.y) <= range end
  return false
end

local SHAPES = {
  [C.VISION.CONE]      = cone,
  [C.VISION.RECTANGLE] = fixed_forward,
  [C.VISION.SQUARE]    = square,
  [C.VISION.LONG_LINE] = fixed_forward,
  [C.VISION.CROSS]     = cross,
}

-- Bresenham line-of-sight: blocked by an obstacle or the food cell (endpoints excluded).
function M.blocked(from, to, is_obstacle, food)
  local x0, y0, x1, y1 = from.x, from.y, to.x, to.y
  local dx, dy = math.abs(x1 - x0), math.abs(y1 - y0)
  local sx = (x0 < x1) and 1 or -1
  local sy = (y0 < y1) and 1 or -1
  local err = dx - dy
  local cx, cy = x0, y0
  while true do
    local is_endpoint = (cx == x0 and cy == y0) or (cx == x1 and cy == y1)
    if not is_endpoint then
      if (is_obstacle and is_obstacle(cx, cy)) or (food and cx == food.x and cy == food.y) then
        return true
      end
    end
    if cx == x1 and cy == y1 then break end
    local e2 = 2 * err
    if e2 > -dy then err = err - dy; cx = cx + sx end
    if e2 < dx then err = err + dx; cy = cy + sy end
  end
  return false
end

function M.can_see(head, player, facing, range, width, vision_type, is_obstacle, food)
  local diff = {x = player.x - head.x, y = player.y - head.y}
  local shape = SHAPES[vision_type] or fixed_forward
  if not shape(diff, facing, range, width) then return false end
  return not M.blocked(head, player, is_obstacle, food)
end

return M
